{{nihongo|'''Awa Shrine'''|安房神社|Awa Jinja|qq=}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] in the Daijingū neighborhood of the city of [[Tateyama, Chiba|Tateyama]] in [[Chiba Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is one of two shrines claiming to hold the title of ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of former [[Awa Province (Chiba)|Awa Province]]. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on August 10.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese|qq=}}</ref>
==Enshrined ''kami''==
The primary ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Awa Jinja is:
*{{nihongo|'''[[Futodama|Ame-no-Futodama-no-mikoto]]'''|天太玉命|qq=}},  the ancestor of Imbe clan
The secondary ''kami'' enshrined at Awa Jinja are:
* {{nihongo|'''Ame-no-hiritome-no-mikoto'''|天乃比理刀咩命|qq=}}, consort of Ame-no-Futodama
*{{nihongo|'''[[Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|Kushiakarutama-no-mikoto]]'''|櫛明玉命|qq=}}, ancestor of the Izumo Imbe clan, the creator of [[Yasakani no Magatama]]
*{{nihongo|'''Ame-no-hiwashi-no-mikoto'''|天日鷲命|qq=}}, ancestor of the Awa Imbe clan
*{{nihongo|'''Taokihooi-no-mikoto'''|手置帆負命|qq=}}, ancestor of the Saga Imbe clan
*{{nihongo|'''Hikosashiri-no-mikoto'''|彦狭知命|qq=}},, ancestor of the Kii Imbe clan
*{{nihongo|'''[[Ame-no-mahitotsu-no-mikoto]]'''|[[天目一箇命]]|qq=}}, ancestor of the [[Tsukushi Province|Tsukushi]] and Ise Imbe clans
==History==
The date of Awa Shrine’s foundation is unknown. Shrine tradition and the ''[[Kogo Shūi]]'' records of 807 AD gives the founder as a member of the [[Inbe clan]],  (the precursors to the [[Nakatomi clan]]) during the reign of the legendary [[Emperor Jimmu]], who settled in this area from [[Awa Province (Tokushima)|Awa Province]] in [[Shikoku]]. The shrine is mentioned several times in the early [[Heian period]] ''[[Rikkokushi]]'' and it is mentioned again in the ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. It was patronized by [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] in the [[Kamakura period]] and was recognized as the ''ichinomiya'' of the province since around this time. The shrine was completely destroyed by a large earthquake in 1499, and was rebuilt in 1593 by [[Satomi Yoshinari]]. The [[Satomi clan]] rebuilt the shrine again in 1536 and around 1592. Subsequently, in the [[Edo Period]] it was granted stipends from the [[Tokugawa shogunate]] in 1616 and 1637. After the [[Meiji Restoration]], the Awa Shrine was designated the Rank of {{nihongo|Imperial shrine, 1st Rank |国幣大社|Kokuhei Taisha|qq=}} under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines]]  under [[State Shinto]] in 1875.<ref>Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125.</ref> The present ''[[Honden]]'' dates from 1881 and was renovated in 2009.<ref name="Yoshiki">{{cite book |last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese|qq=}}</ref>
During archaeological investigations in 1931, numerous [[Jōmon period|Jōmon]] and [[Kofun period]] artifacts were recovered, including a number of [[bronze mirror]]s, clay vessels and the skeletons of 22 people.<ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://www.pref.chiba.lg.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/bunkazai/p411-037.html|title=安房神社洞窟遺跡|trans-title=Abo Shrine Cave Ruins|language=Japanese |publisher=Chiba Prefecture |accessdate=August 20, 2020|qq=}}</ref>
The shrine is a ten-kilometer walk from [[Tateyama Station (Chiba)|Tateyama Station]] on the [[JR East]] [[Uchibo Line]].<ref name="Okada">{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese|qq=}}</ref>
